ratings_why.fun: Voting the water each turn after scouting is a real decision, and the mills paying for every Vote makes the board grow in a way you can feel; the term load keeps it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because no tribe sets one water level that both boards fight in and that judges units by their Health shape, so scouting becomes a choice each turn.

verdict_why: One core rule is unclear: Under says it attacks with half its Attack but not what it deals back when attacked, and that decides most fights.

points.text: Under says a sunk unit attacks with half its Attack, but both units deal damage at once, so a player can't tell whether an Under defender hits back at full or half. Say "deals half its Attack" if both are meant.

Board Almoner reads your Level while Under reads the water, two different lines a player must hold. Consider having the gauge staff show your Level mark and the fight's water mark side by side so the gap is visible.
Seven terms (Level, Vote, water, Flood, Under, Dive, Drowning, plus Overflow) is a lot to read at a glance. Drowning could live only on Tiddy Mun's card, since he is its only source.
Heemraad Old Bram Stuw's "Vote again" doesn't say whether you may pick a new direction; the Seesaw build wants that, so "Vote again, either way" would read cleaner next to Hendrika's "the same way".

The fantasy lands in play: draining pays gold, coots dive and kick at sunk enemies, the mills turn on every motion. The one risk to it is the vote prompt, so a standing Raise/Lower switch is worth building in from the start.

standouts.why: Kees Kowk reads in one line and is pure coot: he kicks at whoever is floundering, even past the front line.
Stretch-Holder is a dike made into a card: the beaver holding his stretch keeps his neighbours above the water.
Master of the Nine Mills is the clearest payoff in the tribe: every Vote turns the mills and the whole board grows.

weakest.why: Keeper of the Overflow inverts the theme, Lowering to raise the water, and adds a private counter; it takes a second read.
Gauge-Keeper's Flood by Level plus half its Health is arithmetic at Start of Combat that a player must redo every fight.
Ditch Coot is fine but plain: Dive plus Flood 1 has no hook of its own beyond sinking itself late.

flags.note: Tiddy Mun with a big Level, Overflow and Gauge-Keeper could drown most of a board at Start of Combat; the half-water rule is the only brake.
Penningmeester with Hendrika and Sluiswacht pays several gold a turn into an uncapped bank.
